basis.rule: Style.space(px) = max(1, round(px * spacingScale * (base-size/12))); Style.fontPx(m) = max(1, round(base-size * m)). At base-size 12 and scale 1.0 every Style.space(n) is n px.
basis.pathsRelativeTo: omarchy repository root at the commit above

items.what: Full-screen wlr-layer-shell surface on the Overlay layer, anchored to all four edges, exclusive keyboard focus, transparent window colour. Namespace omarchy-menu. Opens on the Hyprland-focused monitor.
items.expr: PanelWindow anchors {top,left,bottom,right}; WlrLayer.Overlay; WlrKeyboardFocus.Exclusive; screen = focusedScreen()

items.what: No open/close animation. Content is held at opacity 0 until the output's size and scale are known, then flips to 1 in one frame. Hyprland's layer rule turns off compositor animation for this namespace. Menu.qml contains no Behavior or Animation.
Rectangle filling the whole output behind the card. Clicking it cancels (closes) the menu.
The card is a BorderSurface (a Rectangle with an Omarchy border spec). It is not PopupCard; Menu.qml does not use PopupCard or PopupMenuRow.
Card outer width, normal case
Card outer width while the active menu is trigger.capture.screenrecord, appearance.font or update.kernel. Applies while browsing that menu, including while filtering inside it.
Card width in select/input (dmenu) mode: the caller's payload.width (default 300), scaled.
Minimum distance from card to screen edge: half of Hyprland general:gaps_out. Omarchy default gaps_out is 10.
Card padding on all four sides, inside the border (Style.spacing.panelPadding).

Card border width on all sides. [menu] border-width is unset in the template, so the fallback applies. Drawn inside the card bounds (Qt Rectangle border) or by BorderOverlay, inside the bounds as well.
items.expr: Border.surfaceSpec('menu','border', ..., max(1, Style.space(2))).widths; overridable by [menu] border-width / border-width-top|right|bottom|left

items.what: Distance from the card's outer edge to the content column on each side: border + padding.
items.expr: card.contentTopInset = borderTop + padding (2 + 18), same for right/bottom/left

items.what: Width of the content column (header, list, rows) at the normal card width.
Card corner radius = Hyprland decoration:rounding. Omarchy default is 0. The 'rounded corners' toggle and the solitude theme give 6.

items.what: Card background alpha ([menu] background-alpha).
No shadow. Menu.qml, BorderSurface and OverlayWindow draw none, and Hyprland decoration shadow is off by default.
No blur by default. Only the optional 'Glassy Windows' toggle adds a Hyprland layer rule blurring behind omarchy-menu (ignore_alpha 0.3).
Horizontally centred on the output.

Vertically centred when opened, never closer than gapsOut to the top. On the first filter keystroke or first submenu move, the top edge freezes where it sits, and from then on the card grows and shrinks downward. The freeze clears when the menu closes or the screen changes.
items.expr: centeredTop = max(Style.gapsOut, round((height - cardHeight) / 2)); effectiveCardTop = cardTop >= 0 ? cardTop : centeredTop; freezeCardTop() on setFilter / setActiveMenu

items.what: Card height = padding*2 + header + gap + list height, capped to the screen. The formula leaves the 2 px border out, so the content column is 4 px taller than the space inside the insets and overhangs the bottom inset by 4 px (see notes).
items.expr: min(contentMargin*2 + headerHeight + contentSpacing + visibleRowsHeight, panel.height - gapsOut*2); final card.height = min(that, panel.height - gapsOut - effectiveCardTop)

items.what: Height the list may use: room left below the (frozen or gapsOut) top, capped at 70% of the screen height, and capped by the list height frozen at the first navigation/keystroke. A submenu or result set longer than the starting menu therefore scrolls instead of growing the card.

When rows do not fit, the list height is chosen to end mid-row: the last fully visible row, then rowSpacing, then a 'peek' of the next row. It never ends on a row boundary. An empty list is one base row tall (50).
items.expr: rowPeek = round(baseRowHeight * 0.55) = round(27.5) = 28; height = totals[full-1] + rowSpacing + rowPeek

items.what: A MouseArea covering the card swallows clicks so they do not reach the scrim.
Vertical gap between header and list (Style.spacing.md).

ListView with clip and StopAtBounds (no overscroll). Wheel: pixelDelta.y when the device reports it, else 3 base rows (150 px) per 120-unit notch. The cursor is kept in view with the next row peeking (rowPeek + rowSpacing = 31 px) past it in the direction of travel. Scrolling is instant.
Gradient at the top of the list (background to transparent). Opacity grows linearly with the scrolled distance and is fully on once 28 px are hidden above. Shown only when content overflows.
items.expr: height = min(Style.space(28), listHeight/2); opacity = clamp((contentY - originY) / height, 0, 1)

items.what: Gradient at the bottom of the list (transparent to background). Opacity tracks the distance still hidden below.
items.expr: height = min(Style.space(28), listHeight/2); opacity = clamp((originY + contentHeight - height - contentY) / height, 0, 1)

items.what: In search only, when there are both direct-child matches and deeper matches: a 17 px section header before the first deeper match, holding a 1 px line inset 4 px left and right, vertically centred.
items.expr: dividerHeight = Style.space(17); line height = Style.spacing.hairline (1); margins Style.space(4)

items.what: Empty state, centred in the list area when there are no rows: glyph U+F0209 (nf-md-eye_off) at 28 px, 8 px gap, then a message at 14 px. Both are 320 px wide and centred, so they are wider than the 260 px list. The list area is one base row (50 px) tall and is not clipped, so the 28 px glyph plus 8 plus the message line overflow it.
items.expr: glyph font.pixelSize = Style.font.displayLarge (28); text font.pixelSize = Style.font.title (14); spacing Style.space(8); width Style.space(320)

items.what: One family for everything: $OMARCHY_MENU_FONT if set, else 'monospace', which Omarchy's fontconfig maps to JetBrainsMono Nerd Font. A summon payload's fontFamily overrides it. Row icons use the row's iconFont when set (47 shipped rows use iconFont 'omarchy', a private icon font).

Root rows in order, with their Nerd Font icon codepoints. All are unconditional, and every submenu has unconditionally visible children, so all 10 show. Apps and About are actions (no chevron). The other 8 are submenus (chevron). Apps has provider:'apps' but also an action, so kind is action: Enter runs 'omarchy-shell omarchy.dock apps' (the dock's app grid), not a submenu.

items.what: Root menu at base-size 12 on a screen at least 753 px tall (logical). Rows total 10*50 + 9*3 = 527, so nothing folds. Card is 300 x 603: header y 20-54, list y 60-587, row k top = 60 + 53k, 16 px from list bottom to card bottom. On a 1080 px-tall output, card top = round((1080-603)/2) = 239.

box.what: Header is a transparent Rectangle spanning the content width, with the card radius. It holds only the filter input and its placeholder: no icon, no search glyph, no breadcrumb, no back arrow, no title separate from the placeholder.

filterInput.what: The header is the search field. A borderless, backgroundless TextInput anchored left and right across the header and vertically centred. Text colour menu.text, 16 px, regular weight (font.weight not set), left-aligned at x 0 of the content column (20 px from the card edge). The caret is hidden (empty cursorDelegate) and pinned to the end. Text cannot be selected (append-only). Alt and Super chords are swallowed.

placeholder.what: A Text laid over the input, visible while the filter is empty and no IME preedit is in progress. It reads the active menu's title, or its label when title is unset, followed by U+2026 '…'. At root: 'Go…' (the injected root row's label, from the language catalog, default 'Go'). In a submenu, e.g. 'Appearance…', or for appearance.workspace-layout its title 'Default Workspace Layout…'. In dmenu mode: '<prompt>…'. Same font and size as the input, 0.58 opacity, elided right, vertically centred.

submenuIndication.what: Entering a submenu changes only the placeholder text (and the rows). There is no breadcrumb, path or back affordance in the header. Back is keyboard-only (Backspace or Left on an empty filter), and Escape closes the whole menu.

verticalMetrics.what: The input's and placeholder's own heights are the font's implicit line height; both are centred in the 34 px box. Exact glyph baseline depends on font metrics at runtime.

element.what: Each row is a BorderSurface, full list width (260 at the normal width). Rows are separated by ListView spacing.

height.base.what: Row height without a visible detail line. Used for every row while not filtering.

height.detail.what: Row height when it has a non-empty detail and a filter is active (or in dmenu mode).
height.detail.expr: detailRowHeight = max(Style.space(58), body + caption + rowPaddingX*2) = max(58, 12+10+24)

radius.what: Row corner radius = Style.cornerRadius (Hyprland rounding; 0 by default, 6 with rounded corners).

reservedBorder.what: Left/right inset reserved for the selected-row border. Its width resolves to 0 by default, so offsets below add 0.

icon.what: Icon glyph column: a Text 36 px wide starting 8 px from the row's left edge, glyph centred horizontally, 18 px. Vertically centred on the label line, not on the row. Font = row.iconFont if set, else the menu font.
icon.expr: leftMargin = rowReservedBorderLeft + Style.space(8); width = Style.space(36); font.pixelSize = Style.font.iconLarge = round(12*1.5); y = contentColumn.y + labelText.y + (labelText.height - height)/2

icon.app.what: App rows (from the apps provider, seen in search) show an 18x18 image instead, centred in the same 36 px column (x = 8 + 9 = 17), aspect-fit.

icon.providerCurrent.what: Provider rows (fonts, kernels, languages, power profiles) show '✓' (U+2713) in the icon column for the current value instead of the provider's icon.

label.what: Label Text: starts 6 px right of the icon column (x = 50), or at x = 18 when the row has no icon. It ends 6 px before the trailing column. Single line, elided right, 16 px, Medium weight.
label.expr: contentColumn.left = iconText.right + Style.space(6) | rowReservedBorderLeft + Style.space(18); right = trail.left - Style.space(6); font.pixelSize = Style.font.heading; font.weight = Font.Medium

contentColumn.what: Label and detail stack in a Column, 3 px apart, vertically centred in the row. With the detail hidden, the column is just the label (Qt positioners skip invisible children).

detail.what: Second line under the label, shown only while a filter is active (or in dmenu mode) and the detail is non-empty. 11 px, regular weight, 0.52 opacity, elided right. In search it is the parent path (ancestor labels joined by ' › ' U+203A, from the top level down, root excluded). It is empty for direct children of root. Outside search the row model carries the item's description as detail, but it is never drawn (no shipped item has a description). In RTL languages ' › ' is rewritten to ' ‹ '.

trail.what: Trailing column: a 14 px-wide Row whose right edge is 8 px from the row's right edge (x = 238..252 in a 260 row). It holds only the submenu chevron. A child-count Text exists but is visible:false.

chevron.what: Submenu/link rows show '›' (U+203A), or '‹' in RTL, at 16 px regular weight and 0.36 opacity, left-aligned in the 14 px trail column and vertically centred on the label line. Action rows draw nothing there (empty text, opacity 0). The 0.36 opacity also applies to the selected row.

shortcutHints.what: None. Rows show no keybinding hints.

checked.what: A row whose `checked:` guard succeeded gets ' ✓' (space + U+2713) appended to its label text, in the label's own colour, size and weight. Nothing else changes.

disabled.what: A row whose `disabled:` guard succeeded: whole row at opacity 0.4, ' ✓' appended to its label, arrow pointer instead of a hand, cannot be selected or activated, and left out of search results.

deadDecorations.what: Two elements exist but are visible:false and must not be drawn: a 4 px left accent bar (height row-18, x 8) and a child-count number in the trail.

normal.what: Transparent fill, no border; icon and label in menu.text; chevron menu.text at 0.36.

cursor.what: One state covers both keyboard cursor and hover; there is no separate hover style. Fill menu.selected-background, which is foreground at 0.08 alpha. Icon, label and chevron turn menu.selected-text (accent); the detail line stays menu.text at 0.52. Border = selected-border spec, colour hyprland.active-border-foreground at 0.25, but its width resolves to 0, so no border is visible by default. Radius = cornerRadius (0).

cursor.borderWidthCaveat.what: The selected-border width is read from [menu] selected-border-width, falling back to [menu] border-width, then to 0. A theme that sets [menu] border-width (to thicken the card) therefore also gives selected rows a border of that width.

hover.what: Hovering moves the cursor to the hovered row, but only after real pointer movement (more than 1 px from the last accepted position). After keyboard navigation or a list rebuild the gate is reset, so a stationary pointer under a row does not steal the cursor. After a click opens a submenu, the first pointer sample is allowed, so the row under the pointer is selected. Hand cursor, or arrow on disabled rows.

pressed.what: No pressed state; a click activates immediately.

focus.what: Keyboard focus sits permanently in the hidden-caret filter input, which forwards every key to the key handler first. No focus ring is drawn anywhere.

noCursor.what: If no row is selectable (all disabled), no row is highlighted. The highlight returns as soon as a row becomes selectable.

disabled.what: Opacity 0.4 for the whole row; never takes the cursor.

behaviour.what: Opens at 'root' unless a route is given (an item id or a declared alias, case-insensitive, '_' -> '-'). '', 'go' and 'menu' mean root. A route that resolves to an action runs it without opening. A link is followed to its target. SUPER+SPACE toggles root, SUPER+ESCAPE opens 'system', and the bar button toggles root.
behaviour.source: shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml:22-36, shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml:1019-1035, shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js:203-217, default/hypr/bindings/utilities.lua:1, default/hypr/bindings/utilities.lua:8, shell/plugins/menu/BarWidget.qml:20

behaviour.what: On open: history cleared, filter empty, selectedIndex 0, cursor on. The cursor settles on the first selectable row (at root: Apps). Guards are re-evaluated in the background, and the menu first renders with the previous evaluation's results.

Up / Down move the cursor one selectable row, skipping disabled rows and wrapping at both ends (Up on the first row goes to the last). If the cursor is inactive, Down goes to the first row and Up to the last.
PageUp / PageDown move 6 rows. The index is taken modulo the row count, so paging also wraps (e.g. PageDown on row 8 of 10 lands on row 4).

Enter, keypad Enter and Right arrow (Left under RTL) all activate the cursor row. Right does not just open submenus: it also runs actions. If the cursor is inactive, Enter only settles it on the first selectable row.

Backspace or Left (Right under RTL), only while the filter is empty, goes back: pops the history stack, or goes to the item's parent if the stack is empty. At root it does nothing. Going back resets the filter and puts the cursor on the first row; the previous selection is not restored.
Escape with a non-empty filter clears it and stays in the current menu. With an empty filter it closes the whole menu from any depth; it never steps back one level.

With a non-empty filter: Backspace deletes one character, Ctrl+Backspace deletes the last word (trailing whitespace, then the last run of non-space), Ctrl+U clears. Alt- and Super-modified keys never edit and never type.

Any printable key the handler does not consume goes into the input and becomes the filter. No click into a field is needed. Each change resets the cursor to the first row, freezes the card top, and rebuilds the list. IME composition is supported, and the placeholder hides during preedit.
Delete on an installed-app row (only reachable via search) opens an uninstall confirmation dialog over the card. On other rows it does nothing.
Tab, Home and End have no handler.

The filter searches every descendant of the active menu, at any depth, not just its direct children. At root that is the whole tree, plus provider rows (installed apps, fonts, languages, kernels), which are loaded on the first keystroke. Hidden (`when` false) and disabled rows are excluded. Every whitespace-separated term must match, either as a substring of 'label + last id segment (._- as spaces) + aliases + searchTerms' or as a whole word of the description.

Results come in two groups: direct children of the active menu first, then deeper descendants. When both groups are non-empty, a 17 px hairline divider separates them. Within each group, rows sort by score, ties broken by path. Score tiers: exact label 0 (2 if top level), installed app with the query as a whole word 0, label prefix 10, label contains 30, other name text 40, description words 60, else 80. Submenus get -2, apps -5. The final key is score*1000 + depth*25 + definition order.

Each result's path shows as its detail line (11 px, 0.52 opacity, rows grow to 58 px). The path is the parent chain of labels joined by ' › ' from the top level, e.g. 'Appearance › Menu Bar'. Direct children of root have no detail and stay 50 px. Searching inside a submenu still shows the full path from the top level.
No matches: the list area (50 px) shows the empty-state glyph and 'No matches for “<query>”'.

Activating a submenu or link row (Enter, Right or click) pushes the current menu onto history, switches to the target, clears the filter, puts the cursor on the first row, and freezes the card top. The card then grows or shrinks downward, and the list is capped at the height frozen at the first move. Volatile provider menus re-enumerate on entry.

Activating an action closes the menu immediately, then runs the command detached via bash -lc. A bare 'omarchy-shell shell summon <id> [payload]' is dispatched in-process instead. App rows launch the app.

`when:` false hides the row. A row is hidden only on an explicit false, so before the first evaluation every row shows. A static submenu with no visible descendants hides too. Provider-backed submenus always show.
`checked:` true appends ' ✓' to the label.
`disabled:` true dims the row to 0.4, appends ' ✓', and makes the row unselectable and unsearchable.
Clicking a non-disabled row moves the cursor there and activates it. Clicking the scrim outside the card closes the menu. Clicks on the card background do nothing.

Inside the Apps provider menu (not reachable by navigation at this commit; see notes), rows sort alphabetically by label, case-insensitive. Every other menu keeps JSONC definition order (user overrides keep the original position, and new ids append).
For right-to-left languages the whole overlay is layout-mirrored, the chevron becomes ‹, the path separator becomes ‹, and Left/Right swap meaning.

colors.expr: hyprland_active_border if colors.toml defines it (may be a multi-stop gradient, e.g. hackerman 'rgba(26a269ee) rgba(2ec27eee) 45deg'), else foreground; times border-alpha 1.0
colors.tomlKeys: [menu] border = hyprland.active-border-foreground -> [hyprland] active-border-foreground = {{ shell_gradient hyprland_active_border foreground }}

colors.expr: When there are 2+ colours, the border is a linear gradient with evenly spaced stops. QML angle a maps to CSS linear-gradient((90 + a)deg): 0 is left->right, 45 is top-left->bottom-right. The gradient line length is the same as CSS's.
foreground at opacity 0.52 (unchanged on the selected row)
accent (label, icon and chevron; chevron keeps its 0.36 opacity)

colors.expr: hyprland_active_border (or foreground) at alpha 0.25, width 0 by default, so not visible
whole row at opacity 0.4 (colours as normal)
linear gradient background -> rgba(background, 0) (top), rgba(background, 0) -> background (bottom); uses the composed card background incl. its alpha

background/foreground/accent come from the theme's colors.toml. Missing keys fall back: background <- color0, foreground <- color7, accent <- color4. Built-in defaults when no file loads: fg #cacccc, bg #101315, accent #cacccc.

notes: Bottom padding is 4 px shorter than the top. cardHeight = 2*padding + header + gap + list leaves out the 2 px border on top and bottom, yet the content column starts at border + padding = 20. The list therefore ends 16 px above the card's outer bottom edge (14 px above the border's inner edge), while the header starts 20 px below the outer top edge (18 px inside the border). Source: shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml:140-142, shell/plugins/menu/Menu.qml:1389-1395, shell/Ui/BorderSurface.qml:21-24. The trailing zero-height Item (Menu.qml:1700-1703) adds no spacing because Qt's Column skips zero-size children (Qt documentation, not repo source).
Runtime: Style.cornerRadius comes from hyprctl decoration:rounding (default 0; 6 with the rounded-corners toggle or the solitude theme). It drives the card radius and the row radius.
Runtime: gapsOut = round(general:gaps_out/2), default 5. It only matters when the card would come within 5 px of an edge, i.e. on very short or narrow outputs.

Runtime: vertical text placement (input, placeholder, label, detail, chevron) follows the resolved font's line metrics. Heights here are box heights; glyph baselines are not fixed by the source. The icon and chevron are centred on the label's line box, not the row.

Runtime: the font is 'monospace' resolved by fontconfig (Omarchy maps it to JetBrainsMono Nerd Font in default/fontconfig/conf.avail/50-omarchy.conf:330-337; 'omarchy font set' can change it), unless OMARCHY_MENU_FONT is set.
Runtime: [font] base-size (written by 'omarchy display text size') and [spacing] scale/scale-with-font rescale every size here. With scale-with-font on, spacing multiplies by base-size/12 as well.

Runtime: `when`/`checked`/`disabled` come from an async bash batch run on every open. The menu renders the previous answers first and rebuilds (possibly resizing and re-centring the card, if not yet frozen) when the batch lands. No root row carries a guard, so the root list is stable.
Runtime: labels are translated from default/i18n/<lang>/menu.json (English shown here). The root placeholder word ('Go') also comes from that catalog.
Runtime: the border is a gradient only for themes whose colors.toml defines hyprland_active_border (hackerman, last-horizon, solitude at this commit). Otherwise it is solid foreground.

The root Apps row is an action with no chevron, even though its id is also the 'apps' provider menu. Enter, Right or click runs 'omarchy-shell omarchy.dock apps' (default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc:24). Its app children appear only in search results (with detail 'Apps'). 'omarchy menu summon apps' does not open them either: the route resolves to the action and runs it (Menu.qml:1025-1028). So the Apps provider list is reachable only through search.
Row descriptions are never shown outside search, and the shipped menu defines none (0 of 423 items), so the detail line in practice only ever shows parent paths.
The selected row has no visible border by default. Its border colour is defined (alpha 0.25), but the width falls back through selected-border-width -> border-width -> 0.
PopupMenuRow.qml and PopupCard.qml (the dock/bar popup style: 28 px rows, Style.hoverFill, right-aligned accent ✓) are not used by the menu. Do not borrow their metrics.

Unresolved: how Qt's ListView places the 17 px section header relative to the 3 px row spacing. This spec follows Menu.qml's own height model (spacing + divider + row, Menu.qml:218-224); the pixel placement inside ListView was not verified against Qt.

Unresolved: the empty-state block (28 px glyph + 8 + ~14 px text line) is taller than the 50 px list area it is centred in, so it overflows above and below by an amount that depends on font metrics. It is not clipped, since only the ListView clips.

Out of scope but present: select/input (dmenu) mode reuses the card with caller width/maxHeight, always-visible subtext, ○/✓ checkbox icons and an 'Apply' row for multi-select (Menu.qml:634-704, 977-1005, docs/menu.md:168-186).
